# Govern AI model access

The AI Inference Gateway governs agent access to large language models (LLMs) in Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric. Agents send requests to one gateway instead of to each provider. The gateway routes each request to a model registered in the Consul catalog and applies policy for failover and sensitive data.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To deploy a gateway, refer to [Configure the AI Inference Gateway](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/model-access/configure).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Introduction

The gateway accepts OpenAI-compatible requests and translates supported operations to the selected provider's format. Agents reach the gateway over the Consul service mesh, so mesh identity and service intentions control which agents can call it and which models it can reach.

Three parts of the gateway share the work:

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| Consul | Supplies the gateway configuration and the models eligible for each capability, from the catalog. |
| Envoy | Enforces mesh policy, selects the upstream model, and retries across failover tiers. |
| External processor | Validates and transforms requests and responses, applies PII protection, and records usage. It does not select routes or retry. |

## How it works

1. An agent sends an OpenAI-compatible request to the gateway over its mesh upstream.
1. **Before routing**, the processor resolves the caller's workload identity, validates the request, and applies request-side PII protection.
1. **Envoy routes** the request to the highest-priority tier of models that serve the requested capability.
1. **After routing**, the processor translates the request for the selected model's provider and rewrites the provider path.
1. If the attempt fails with a retriable error, Envoy retries the next tier. The processor translates the request again for that tier's model.
1. **On the response**, the processor normalizes supported responses, applies response-side PII protection, and records usage before the response returns to the agent.

The [Govern model access](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/architecture#govern-model-access) diagram on the architecture page shows this flow.

## Model routing and failover

The gateway routes each request in one of two modes:

| Mode | How the gateway routes | When it applies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capability routing | On the capability named in the `x-inference-specialization` request header | Default |
| Body model routing | On the model named in the request body | When body model routing is turned on |

The Consul catalog decides which models serve a capability and in what order. Each model service declares its capabilities and a priority for each one. Models with the same priority form a tier and share load. A request whose capability no model serves fails closed.

When two or more tiers serve a capability, Envoy fails a request over from one tier to the next. You control which errors trigger a retry, how many tiers one request can try, and the timeout for each attempt.

Provider translation changes the request format. It does not make two models equivalent in capability, quality, or data-handling terms.

### Supported model protocols

Each model service declares the API dialect it serves: `openai`, `anthropic`, or `passthrough`. The default is `openai`.

To declare the protocol, refer to [Register model services](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/model-access/configure#register-model-services).

## Data protection and streaming

The gateway detects personally identifiable information (PII) in request and response content and handles each match according to your policy. Request-side protection acts before data reaches a provider. Response-side protection acts before content returns to the agent.

- **Detectors.** Use the built-in `api_key`, `credit_card`, `email`, and `ssn` detectors, or define a custom detector with an RE2 regular expression. The `credit_card` detector also checks the Luhn digit.
- **Actions.** Replace each match with a placeholder, mask it, block the request, or ignore it. The actions are `placeholder`, `mask`, `block`, and `off`.
- **Scope.** Scan requests, responses, or both. The default is requests.
- **Streaming.** The gateway withholds a configurable number of trailing bytes from a streamed response, so that it catches a match split across chunks.

Metrics and decision logs record bounded metadata only. They never include prompts, responses, detected PII values, credentials, or provider error text that can contain request content. Payload traces that carry content need separate approval and redaction. Refer to the [auto-instrumentation privacy controls](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation#payload-span-sensitive-data-security).

## Configuration fields

On Kubernetes, you configure a gateway with an `InferencePoolConfig` resource. The controller writes the supported fields to the gateway's [`inference-gateway` configuration entry](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/inference-gateway).

| Setting | `InferencePoolConfig` field | Configuration entry field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Processor failure mode. The controller defaults it to `closed`. | `processor.failureMode` | `Processor.FailureMode` |
| Body model routing | `processor.bodyModelRouting` | `Processor.BodyModelRouting` |
| Failover tiers, retry conditions, and per-attempt timeout | `routing.fallback` | `Failover` |
| PII detection, actions, scope, and stream holdback | `policy.pii` | `PII` |
| Metrics and tracing | `observability` | `Observability` |
| Deadline for the whole request across every attempt | None in Consul 2.1 | `RequestTimeout` |

In Consul 2.1, the controller ignores other `InferencePoolConfig` fields, including `routing.timeout` and `rateLimit`. Refer to the [`InferencePoolConfig` reference](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/inferencepoolconfig).

## Observability

The gateway [automatically instruments supported model exchanges](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation), so applications do not need tracing SDKs. Tracing is off by default. To turn it on, refer to [Enable AI Inference Gateway tracing](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation#enable-ai-inference-gateway-tracing).

Gateway traces also feed [cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection), which needs Agentic Analytics in addition to tracing.

## Limitations

- OpenAI compatibility does not mean every provider feature works, or that models behave the same.
- PII detection covers the configured detectors only. It does not guarantee that all sensitive content is found. Validate detector coverage and streaming behavior for your deployment.
- Content already streamed to the agent cannot be recalled.
- Authentication to managed model providers is separate from on-behalf-of delegation and external credential injection.
- The gateway does not run tool logic or judge whether a model response completes the user's task.
